name: 2112 Prairie Avenue (the Rothschild house): the brick barn on the alley between its neighbours' coach houses, K12

function.note: Sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn draws a two-storey brick building on the alley behind 2112 and letters it AUTO. AUTO is a 1911 use and is not read as the 1904 one (the K12 kit's restriction no_1911_use_labels; T-1837 study ruling 11). The T-1842 sheet census (row s35-2112-rear) carries the building into 1904 as the Rothschild stable, on the Chicago Daily Tribune's classified of 31 May 1910 (image record nps-2112-tribune-1910-05-31-brick-barn-to-rent: 'To Rent—2112 Prairie-av., brick barn; rental $40'), which shows a brick barn standing on the lot a year before the sheet. INFERRED: the barn of 1910 carried back to 1904 as the stable and coach house; no source read names a horse or a carriage on this lot in 1904, and the Tribune item is not yet a source record.

research_note: T-1937 refines the district draft (T-2351) in place under the same id onto the K12 coach-house kit. The sheet census (row s35-2112-rear, trace s35fp-2112-b2) carries the building into 1904; the draft rules now skip that row. Read afresh off the committed sheet 35 raster by darkness profiles (2100's and 2108/2110's method) rather than taken from the draft's fitted rectangle, which had stood it 13.0 m along the alley and 8.5 m deep under a gable, its north 0.4 m and south 1.5 m short of the walls the sheet draws: the sheet draws one plain rectangle on the alley line, 8.62 m deep and 14.50 m between its own north and south wall lines, with no roof line, wing or porch on it, a fire-wall sign at the alley end of both walls and two of the key's window marks on its alley wall. Its north wall stands on the line the sheet draws once with 2108 and 2110's shared coach house; its south wall stands two pixels (0.37 m) from 2120's alley building. Neither picture T-1937's image gate names for it shows it: Chicagology's c. 1895 view along the west side from 2110 and the Glessner House blog's 1890s print of the 2100 block's west side show the house fronts on Prairie Avenue, and the alley buildings stand behind them; no camera is solved.

documented_range.note: The draft's claim, kept: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped), the Rothschild stable, a brick barn to rent in May 1910. TO is the last day of the year the sheet was published, the latest date anything read here shows it standing; it is not a demolition date.

footprint.note: About the middle of the alley wall, u east (toward the street) and v north. Depth 8.62 m: the alley line (column 474.00) to the yard wall line (median centroid 520.36 over the same rows), 46.36 pixels at the sheet's 0.185854 m a pixel. Length 14.75 m along the alley: the sheet's own two wall lines stand 78.0 pixels apart (rows 1208.0 and 1286.0), 14.50 m; the north end is carried 0.25 m on to 2108 and 2110's committed south face (see the position note), so the two stand on one line as the sheet draws them. A plain rectangle: the sheet draws no step, wing, porch or roof line on it, 128.8 m2 against the trace's 118.2 m2 fill (the trace's notch at the north-east corner is the storey figure '2' lettered there, not a wall). The sheet's fire-wall sign stands at the alley end of both the north and the south wall, so both ends are built as party walls (east_end party), as 1824 and 2011 Prairie's are; their returns stand 0.5 m past the eaves, which is the kit's and not the sheet's. The north party wall stands inside this outline, back to back with 2108 and 2110's own south wall.

stories.note: '2' lettered in the building's north-east corner: two storeys. Built as the kit's carriage room (3.6 m) under a loft whose walls rise 2.7 m more to the eave, under the kit's 40-degree gable (3.6 m from eave to ridge over the 8.62 m span), its ridge along the alley between the two party walls; those heights and the roof are RECONSTRUCTED: the sheet draws no roof line on this building, where it draws 2100's hip and deck, so it stands under the kit's own roof.

construction.note: Drawn pink, the sheet's colour for brick, on the whole rectangle, with a wall thickness lettered inside its north and south walls. The kit builds its own 13-inch walls in its own brick colour.

value.note: Everything but the plan, the two storeys, the brick, the two party walls and the two window marks' places is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-2112-barn-1937. The sheet draws ONE rectangle on the alley line, 8.62 m deep, lettered AUTO with '2' storeys, standing between 2108 and 2110's coach house (on one line with it) and 2120's alley building (0.37 m off), with the key's fire-wall sign at the alley end of both walls, so both ends are party walls and there is no open gable. On the alley wall the sheet draws two of the key's window marks (a cross with a dot for each storey, as on 2011's and 1824's alley walls), centred 2.69 m and 11.43 m south of the north wall line (rows 1222.5 and 1269.5): each is built as a stable sash with a loft sash over it. s counts on the alley wall from the north party wall's inner face (the marks at 2.61 and 11.35) and on the yard wall from the south party wall's. Between the marks the kit lays a carriage bay 3.0 m clear under the loft hatch and hoist, and a man door with a loft sash over it; the yard wall has a door toward the house and three stable sash, a loft sash over each. The ends are blank party walls. AUTO is the 1911 use; nothing of a motor garage is built.

coach_house.note: The K12 kit's coach house on the plan, storeys, brick, party walls and window marks the 1911 sheet draws; see the value's note.
